content: I'll split this bead into 4 focused child beads, ordered from diagnosis to fixes to safeguards.

args.command:
bead create --title "Isolate the hang source in vitest workers" --description "Identify what handle, timer, or worker thread keeps the Node event loop alive after tests finish.

The vitest suite exits 124 (timeout) despite all vitest timeout flags (--testTimeout, --hookTimeout, --teardownTimeout). This means a worker refuses to exit after test completion - an open handle (socket, timer, worker thread, or OPFS mock handle) is blocking graceful shutdown.

## Task
- Use Node.js debugging tools to identify active handles after test completion
- Check the OPFS mock in test/setup.ts as a likely suspect (jsdom environment)
- Identify which specific resource prevents the event loop from draining
- Document the finding with stack traces and handle types

## Acceptance Criteria
- Identify the exact handle type (timer/socket/worker/OPFS handle) keeping workers alive
- Provide a minimal repro showing the hang trigger
- Document why vitest timeouts don't catch it (they abort test bodies, not worker lifecycle)
" --label split-child
args.description: Create first child bead for isolating the hang source

args.command:
bead create --title "Fix the GB-scale memory leak in vitest workers" --description "Stop the heap growth that causes workers to reach 1.9-2.6 GB RSS within seconds.

A vitest worker reached 1.9 GB RSS at 13 seconds old, with another node process at 2.6 GB. This is Node heap exhaustion, not system memory pressure (52 GB available, zero swap). The leak compounds across the 12-worker pool and eventually exhausts the host.

## Task
- Profile heap growth during test runs (use Node.js heap snapshots or --heap-prof)
- Identify the leak source (likely in test fixtures, OPFS mock, or vitest worker setup)
- Apply a fix that stops unbounded growth
- Verify workers stay under a reasonable RSS ceiling (e.g., <500 MB) during a full suite run

## Acceptance Criteria
- Identify and patch the leak source
- Full suite runs without workers exceeding 500 MB RSS sustained
- No swap usage or OOM symptoms on the test host
" --label split-child
args.description: Create second child bead for fixing memory leak

args.command:
bead create --title "Implement process group cleanup to kill orphans" --description "Fix the orphaned worker problem: children survive parent death and run for hours.

Current behavior: \`timeout(1) npm test\` sends SIGTERM to the parent command, but the vitest worker pool and esbuild children reparent to systemd and continue running. One orphaned test ran 13 hours holding 12 workers plus a spinning esbuild. This exhausts fork/task resources and wedges the server.

## Task
- Change the kill mechanism from targeting the command to targeting the PROCESS GROUP
- Ensure all children (workers, esbuild, subprocess trees) receive termination signals
- Test with \`timeout(1)\` and verify full cleanup
- Update CI configs (scripts, package.json, Argo workflows) to use process group killing

## Acceptance Criteria
- \`timeout(1) npm test\` kills all children - no orphans remain
- Process group killing verified across environments (local, CI)
- Updated all CI configs to use process-aware termination
- Document the pattern for future Node.js projects
" --label split-child
args.description: Create third child bead for process group cleanup

args.command:
bead create --title "Add CI safeguards and monitoring for test hangs" --description "Prevent future test suite hangs from wedging servers or exhausting resources.

Once the hang and leak are fixed, add defense-in-depth safeguards to catch regressions early and limit damage.

## Task
- Add timeout guards at the PROCESS GROUP level (not vitest level)
- Add RSS/memory caps to prevent runaway heap growth
- Add orphan detection/alerting (check for stray node processes after test completion)
- Update package.json scripts with proper wrappers
- Document the safeguards for contributors

## Acceptance Criteria
- Test invocations terminate cleanly within a bounded wall-clock timeout
- Memory caps prevent heap exhaustion even if a leak returns
- Orphaned processes trigger immediate alerts and auto-cleanup
- Contributing guide explains the safeguards and why they exist
" --label split-child
args.description: Create fourth child bead for CI safeguards
